nodes.content: Develop video-language grounding that distinguishes repeated actions through temporal relationships while remaining robust to irrelevant visual changes.
requirements: Ground both queries correctly in 80% of event-order minimal pairs (temporal IoU ≥0.5).
Limit accuracy loss to 5 percentage points under background changes preserving actions and timing.

nodes.content: Train OrderBind with contrastive learning on order-swapped queries over event-instance spans and background-swap consistency for robust localization.
Does OrderBind’s background-swap consistency collapse temporally distinct instances of the same action into interchangeable grounding targets?
Instance-aligned background-swap positives should maintain ≥0.15 cosine distance between repeated-action spans, versus <0.05 under action-label pairing.
Build OrderSwap-500 with paired background edits; compare instance-aligned versus action-label consistency using repeated-span cosine distance and paired grounding accuracy.
Train OrderBind with instance-aligned or action-label positives; evaluate repeated-span cosine distance and paired grounding accuracy on OrderSwap-500 background edits.
OrderSwap-500: repeated-span cosine distance was 0.18 instance-aligned versus 0.04 action-label; paired accuracy was 83% clean, 80% background-edited.
Use e1’s 0.18-versus-0.04 separation to set a 0.10 collapse cutoff, then measure both variants on held-out OrderSwap-500 scene swaps.
Held-out OrderSwap-500 scene swaps reduced instance-aligned cosine distance to 0.08 (<0.10 collapse cutoff) and paired accuracy from 82% to 74%.
Retain instance-aligned positives given e1’s strong results, but add cross-scene, same-action instance negatives to address e2’s eight-point accuracy loss.
Cross-scene same-action instance negatives will raise held-out repeated-span cosine distance above 0.15 and limit paired-accuracy loss to ≤5 points.
Retrain OrderBind with cross-scene same-action instance negatives; test held-out OrderSwap-500 swaps for cosine separation and clean-to-edited paired accuracy.
With cross-scene negatives, held-out OrderSwap-500 repeated-span cosine distance reached 0.17; both-query accuracy (tIoU≥0.5) was 85% clean, 82% edited.
Does OrderBind use relative event order or shortcut on absolute timestamps when repeated actions shift within a video?
Using e3’s checkpoint, compare OrderSwap-500 both-query accuracy (tIoU≥0.5) before and after time-shifting action pairs without changing event order.
OrderSwap-500 ShiftSet: paired original/time-shifted clips, unchanged-order annotations, and a script reporting both-query tIoU≥0.5 accuracy by shift.
Train RelGraphGround to match query-derived before/after graphs against action proposals using motion features and adversarial background suppression.
How sensitive is RelGraphGround’s before/after matching to missed brief anchor actions in its proposal graph?
Omitting anchor actions shorter than 0.6 seconds will reduce RelGraphGround’s both-query accuracy (tIoU≥0.5) by at least 12 percentage points.
On ShiftSet’s annotated clips, remove anchor proposals shorter than 0.6 seconds; compare RelGraphGround both-query accuracy (tIoU≥0.5) against intact graphs.
ShiftSet short-anchor clips: RelGraphGround both-query accuracy (tIoU≥0.5) fell from 81% to 76% after removal, only five points.
Removing brief anchors lowers accuracy by ≤5 points with another temporal anchor available, but ≥12 points without one.
Stratify e4’s ShiftSet clips by surviving temporal anchors; remeasure RelGraphGround’s both-query accuracy drop after brief-anchor removal in each stratum.
ShiftSet both-query accuracy (tIoU≥0.5) fell 83%→80% with surviving anchors (n=180), versus 72%→58% without them (n=40).
Adopt OrderBind with cross-scene negatives as primary: 85% clean/82% edited accuracy, avoiding RelGraphGround’s 14-point no-anchor drop.
Keep OrderBind primary; fuse RelGraphGround scores only with ≥2 detected anchors, then test paired accuracy and background robustness on OrderSwap-500.
Implement two-anchor-gated score fusion; compare it with OrderBind alone on OrderSwap-500 clean and background-edited both-query accuracy (tIoU≥0.5).
AnchorGate v1: two-anchor-gated OrderBind–RelGraphGround fusion module with OrderSwap-500 clean and background-edited both-query evaluation scripts.
Run AnchorGate v1 scripts on OrderSwap-500, comparing fusion, OrderBind, and RelGraphGround both-query accuracy (tIoU≥0.5) on clean and background-edited clips.
On OrderSwap-500 unseen-object edits, RelGraphGround scored 82%→80%, OrderBind 85%→77%, and AnchorGate 86%→83% both-query accuracy (tIoU≥0.5).
Do moving background objects create false temporal anchors that mislead RelGraphGround and AnchorGate despite the two-anchor gate?
Extend e6’s unseen-object edits with action-preserving moving distractors; run AnchorGate v1 and RelGraphGround, measuring false-anchor rates and paired accuracy.
Moving-distractor OrderSwap-500: RelGraphGround false-anchor rate reached 29%; clean→edited both-query accuracy fell 82%→69%, and AnchorGate 86%→76% (tIoU≥0.5).
Disable AnchorGate fusion for moving distractors (76% edited accuracy); retain it for unseen-object edits (83%).
Train ActorTrace to ground query-relative action intervals from actor-object tracks, masking distractor motion and enforcing background-swap consistency.
Can ActorTrace preserve event-order grounding when brief occlusions fragment the queried actor’s track?
ActorTrace’s track stitching should limit both-query accuracy loss to ≤5 points when actor occlusions last ≤0.8 seconds.
Under d3’s no-fusion moving-distractor setting, compare ActorTrace both-query accuracy (tIoU≥0.5) before and after ≤0.8-second actor occlusions.
On moving-distractor OrderSwap-500 clips, ≤0.8-second occlusions reduced ActorTrace both-query accuracy (tIoU≥0.5) from 83% to 74%.
Under d3’s no-fusion policy, stratify e8’s occluded clips by stitched-track ID switches and gap duration; remeasure both-query accuracy.
Stratification exposed an ID-switch evaluation bug; corrected ActorTrace accuracy fell 83%→79% across all ≤0.8-second occlusions.
Will actor-object tracks stay aligned with queries when similar-looking actors exchange objects during repeated actions?
Augment e8’s clips with similar-actor object exchanges; apply e9’s corrected ID-switch evaluator to compare ActorTrace and OrderBind paired accuracy.
Use AnchorGate v1 evaluation scripts to score ActorTrace and OrderBind on similar-actor object exchanges with corrected ID-switch annotations.
ExchangeSwap-200: 200 paired similar-actor object-exchange clips with corrected track IDs, order-swapped queries, and both-query tIoU≥0.5 scoring.
Benchmark ActorTrace against OrderBind on ExchangeSwap-200, auditing corrected track IDs and both-query accuracy (tIoU≥0.5) across object exchanges.
ExchangeSwap-200 both-query accuracy (tIoU≥0.5): ActorTrace 82% versus OrderBind 73%; corrected track IDs stayed aligned in 91% of exchanges.
Adopt ActorTrace for actor-exchange clips: 82% versus OrderBind’s 73%; corrected occlusion scoring shows a four-point loss, not nine.
Train StateChain to match query order against object-state transitions, using foreground-preserving scene swaps to suppress background shortcuts.
Can StateChain distinguish repeated actions when the object returns to the same state between occurrences?
Relative-order edges will let StateChain ground identical object-state cycles with ≥80% both-query accuracy (tIoU≥0.5).
Create identical-state-cycle variants of ExchangeSwap-200; compare StateChain with and without relative-order edges on both-query accuracy (tIoU≥0.5).
On ExchangeSwap-200 identical-state cycles, StateChain reached 72% both-query accuracy (tIoU≥0.5) with relative-order edges versus 59% without.
Adding actor-contact onset nodes to StateChain’s order graph will raise identical-state-cycle both-query accuracy from 72% to ≥80%.
Use e11’s 72% baseline; annotate contact onsets, add them to StateChain’s order graph, and retest identical-state-cycle pairs.
On ExchangeSwap-200 identical-state cycles, compare StateChain without order edges, with order edges, and with actor-contact onsets using both-query accuracy (tIoU≥0.5).
After longer training, identical-state-cycle accuracy was 60% without order edges, 81% with edges, and 77% adding contact-onset nodes.
Reconcile 72% versus 81% order-edge results through matched-epoch contact-onset ablations on ExchangeSwap-200 corrected tracks, measuring both-query tIoU≥0.5 accuracy.
Matched-epoch, manually adjudicated onsets raised StateChain both-query accuracy (tIoU≥0.5) to 84% versus 81% order-only, surpassing e11’s 72% baseline.
Can automatically detected contact onsets preserve StateChain’s 84% both-query accuracy under moving-distractor backgrounds?
Calibrate automatic onsets using e13’s adjudications; compare clean/moving-distractor both-query accuracy against e12’s 77% uncorrected-onset and e13’s 84% curated-onset baselines.
Calibrate contact-onset detector against ExchangeSwap-200 corrected tracks; generate action-preserving moving-distractor edits for clean-versus-edited StateChain scoring.
ExchangeSwap-200 v2 adds action-preserving moving-distractor clips and calibrated contact-onset predictions to v1’s corrected-track, order-swapped pairs.
Audit ExchangeSwap-200 v2 onset predictions and measure StateChain’s clean-versus-moving-distractor both-query accuracy (tIoU≥0.5) using automatic onsets.
ExchangeSwap-200 v2: automatic-onset StateChain achieved 83% clean and 80% moving-distractor both-query accuracy (tIoU≥0.5), a three-point loss.
Adopt calibrated-onset StateChain: matched-epoch testing supports 81% order-only and 84% adjudicated-onset accuracy; automatic onsets retain 83%→80% under distractors.
